simple: Firmware whose main function is one endless loop that does every job in turn.
analogy: One teacher alone in a one-room school, working down the same list all day.
precise: A bare-metal program structure in which all application work runs in one loop in thread context, often woken by a timer tick or other interrupts that only set flags or count; a job's start time depends on how long every job before it in the loop takes.
source: D3 of BR-05 (Elecia White, Making Embedded Systems; title only, pending verification) and R1 of BR-05 (lab run bm_superloop)

simple: How long after the planned moment an output was actually written.
analogy: How many seconds after the minute the heater was set.
precise: For a periodic step k with release time k·T: the time stamp taken right after the actuator write minus k·T. It includes the wake-up delay and the step's own execution time; its spread (maximum minus minimum) is reported as the loop's jitter.
source: R1 and R5 of BR-05 (lab runs; definition used by the lab programs)

simple: The state the processor is in while it runs an interrupt handler; there is no task to put to sleep.
analogy: Answering the doorbell: you cannot go home and come back tomorrow while standing at the door.
precise: Code running as an exception or interrupt handler (Handler mode on Armv7-M), entered by hardware on top of the interrupted code; it must not block, because the interrupted code and everything of equal or lower priority cannot run until the handler returns.
source: D1 and D4 of BR-05 (Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual; Zephyr and FreeRTOS documentation; titles only, pending verification); R3 of BR-05 (lab run trap_isr_block)

simple: A stretch of code during which the processor ignores interrupts.
analogy: A group that locks the hall door from the inside: nobody can enter, not even the most urgent group.
precise: Code between disabling and re-enabling interrupts (on Armv7-M, cpsid i and cpsie i, which set and clear PRIMASK); interrupts that arrive meanwhile stay pending, so the tick and the scheduler are delayed by the whole section. Its longest instance is a blocking term in every task's response time.
source: D1 and D7 of BR-05 (Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual; Buttazzo; titles only, pending verification); R2 of BR-05 (forensic run)

simple: A small hardware guard that can forbid code from touching some memory regions, without translating addresses.
analogy: Staff-only signs that the building enforces, in a building with one set of room numbers.
precise: An optional Armv7-M unit that checks every access against a few programmable regions with permissions and raises a fault on a violation; unlike an MMU it has no page tables and no separate address spaces.
source: D1 and D2 of BR-05 (Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual; Yiu; titles only, pending verification)

simple: How much memory a piece of software needs to run.
analogy: How many rooms and cupboards a school needs.
precise: For firmware, the sizes of code (.text, in flash) and data (.data and .bss, in RAM) reported by the linker or a size tool; for a Linux process, its virtual size and resident set (VmSize and VmRSS in /proc/self/status), plus the kernel and libraries it relies on.
source: D6 of BR-05 (proc(5) manual page; title only, pending verification); R9 of BR-05 (footprint run)
